query: (Cathay MD) Build a model to organise/optimise routes and service so Overall Rating > 7.

per_column.name: Service_Quality_Score
per_column.rationale: Appears to be a composite (average) of the existing service sub-ratings (Seat Comfort, Staff Service, Food & Beverages, Inflight Entertainment). This is a sound computation on original numeric columns, so it is grounded, and the pattern (row 1 terrible narrative and row 3 glowing narrative both ~3.75, while row 4 hits 5.0) confirms it reflects numeric ratings rather than text sentiment. As an aggregate it gives a single service axis for modelling but is substantially redundant with the individual rating columns and highly collinear with the Overall Rating target, capping its added leverage. Values cannot be text-verified from the samples (underlying numeric columns not shown), a mild groundedness caveat.

per_column.name: Service_to_Value_Gap
per_column.rationale: Consistent with Service_Quality_Score minus Value_For_Money (e.g., row 4: 5.0 service, gap 1.0 -> value 4; row 3: 3.75 service, gap -1.25 -> value 5). This is a genuinely new axis: it isolates the mismatch between perceived service and perceived value, which is directly actionable for a route/service optimisation model rather than a mere restatement of either input. Derived from existing numeric columns, so well grounded, though not independently text-verifiable in the samples.

per_column.name: Route_Complexity
per_column.rationale: Counts route segments/connections from the Route field (row 1 'Manchester to Sydney via Hong Kong' = 2, row 5 'Beijing to Bangkok via Hong Kong' = 2, row 2 'Hong Kong to Tokyo' = 1). Cleanly extracted and verifiable from source text. Highly relevant to a route-optimisation query: direct vs connecting is a distinct grouping/modelling axis not captured by any existing column.

per_column.name: Business_Traveller
per_column.rationale: Binary flag that essentially one-hot-encodes the existing 'Type of Traveller' categorical column, so it is largely a trivial restatement of original data with limited new leverage. Values cannot be confirmed from the shown text (Type of Traveller not in samples) but are derivable from an existing column; no hallucination observed. Provides a mild segmentation axis but low novelty.

per_column.name: Premium_Class
per_column.rationale: Binarisation of the existing 'Class' column (premium cabins vs not). Verifiable rows match the text: row 4 mentions 'Economy' -> 0, row 5 mentions 'business class A330' -> 1, row 3 (economy) -> 0. Well grounded. As a feature it is a somewhat redundant recoding of Class, but cabin tier is a relevant grouping axis for service optimisation, so moderate usefulness.

per_column.name: High_Satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Binary satisfaction flag that tracks the sentiment/Overall Rating (positive reviews rows 3,4 = 1; negative rows 1,2,5 = 0), i.e. essentially a thresholded restatement of the existing Overall Rating target. Grounded, but as a model feature it is target leakage and as a label it merely duplicates the existing target column, so its independent analytical value is limited.

judge.rationale: The set mixes genuinely useful new axes with redundant recodings. Route_Complexity and Service_to_Value_Gap add real analytical leverage for a route/service optimisation model, and Service_Quality_Score offers a service summary (though collinear with the target). Business_Traveller, Premium_Class, and especially High_Satisfaction are largely binarisations/restatements of existing columns, with High_Satisfaction effectively duplicating the Overall Rating target. Groundedness is strong overall: verifiable columns (Route_Complexity, Premium_Class, High_Satisfaction) match the source text, and the remaining scores are sound computations over existing numeric/categorical columns; no clear hallucinations were observed in the samples, only an inability to independently text-verify the rating-derived aggregates.
